body:
## Purpose and acceptance status

Provide reproducible evidence against the **complete accepted retained-view hosting contract**. This is ordinary validation work outside the Wayfinder decision map. It is the continuing runtime acceptance gate, separate from [Approve the combined-window design with runtime feasibility unproven](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/22). Under the [creator-approved decision-only completion boundary](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/22#issuecomment-6478721978), this issue no longer blocks design-map closure. Design approval does not satisfy this gate, certify feasibility, waive any requirement or authorize a production merge.

**No Stage 1 pass or overall feasibility pass currently exists.** Do not add historical sampled results from different commits together and call that a current-source pass. Implementation completion is also not a validation result.

The creator has [retained the candidate provisionally and recorded the accumulated experiment as incomplete with scoped repair evidence](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/33#issuecomment-6478428043). That investment/experiment verdict is complete; it is not a runtime acceptance pass. [Complete the disposable retained-view hosting integration](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/34) owns missing code. This validation gate cannot close until necessary integration, required evidence and a separate live creator verdict are complete. Bounded investigation may continue after a failed prerequisite where authorized; later-stage acceptance still requires earlier gates to pass.

## Canonical requirements and preserved history

- [Final audited design approval and profile-target clarification](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/22#issuecomment-6478807512): design-map approval is complete with runtime feasibility explicitly unproven. Include the exact-workspace/explicit-profile reuse, project-scoped change and cancellation scenario in opening/profile validation; design approval is not a runtime result.
- [Frozen complete inherited acceptance contract](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/33#issuecomment-6478223824): the entire pre-consolidation body is preserved verbatim. **No substantive requirement is removed by this reorganization.** Historical pending-status text is not a new verdict, and historical stop-on-failure directions remain superseded by the creator's accepted policy: failures block acceptance, not investigation or repair.
- [Validate the selected hosting architecture with live workbenches](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/23): original three stages and evidence/verdict requirements.
- [Revalidate live workbench hosting after IPC refinement](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/25): original explicit native-service boundary matrix.
- [Choose how independent project workbenches share one window](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/20): all creator-accepted identity, lifetime, reply, recovery, Close, disposal and readiness refinements.
- [Define project ownership and navigation for chats](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/17), [Define project tab lifecycle and background activity](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/18), [Define fresh-app startup, opening and recovery behavior](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/24): the accepted product contract.
- [Consolidated evidence review](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/33#issuecomment-6478224295): what the accumulated experiments demonstrate and what they leave unperformed. Existing detailed reports remain evidence assets, not blanket passes.

The grouped inventory below is a navigation aid to that full contract. If a detail is absent here, its absence does not waive the frozen or linked requirement. A discrepancy must be surfaced, not silently resolved in favour of a weaker checklist.

## Stage 1 — hosting, identity, isolation and lifecycle

### V1. Current-source native/generic/direct boundary coverage

- [ ] Pin the exact source/build/runtime; boot real Agents, single-folder and saved multi-folder workbenches inside one host. Record native-host, logical-workbench, workspace/environment and actual renderer/process identities and destinations.
- [ ] Complete role/target/service/event/reply/port coverage: authenticated actual sender, caller arguments and handshake spoofing, explicit/nested/auxiliary targets, registered auxiliary ownership, internal/shared-role separation and legitimate named shell/Agents/project coordinator operations. Selection must never authenticate background requests.
- [ ] Exercise main-owned document and connection generations across initial/replacement bootstrap, reused Electron objects, reconnect, reload/navigation, crash and disposal. Reject stale handles, readiness, subscriptions and replies explicitly while fresh authorized controls succeed. Tab switching/same-document activity must not spuriously revoke access; a vetoed reload preserves current authority.
- [ ] Cover revocation during asynchronous work: no unauthorized late effect/publication/event/reply/port into a replacement; clean renderer-owned late resources, preserve independent provider work, and make no rollback claim for completed effects. Connection replacement cannot revive expired ownership.
- [ ] Include direct diagnostics, shared/PTY/agent-host ports, agent-host restart/policy, auxiliary parent registration, startup objects/config/environment, zoom/DevTools/raw reload and delayed native-menu callbacks, plus relevant newly discovered native/main boundaries and downstream scopes. Prior inventories and sampled adapters are starting points, not an exhaustive audit. Use isolated diagnostic connections or relaunch after probes replacing ordinary IPC.

### V2. Real safeguards and authoritative lifecycle outcomes

- [ ] Exercise genuine Save / Don't Save / Cancel, Hot Exit/backups, failed save/backup, shutdown joiners and terminal/task/debug confirmation with real work. Preserve recoverable edits; a not-ready renderer is not permission to discard work. Correct incomplete adapters before claiming their requirements passed.
- [ ] Bind lifecycle replies to exact sender/workbench/document, pending operation and expected phase before consuming listeners. Test own success/veto/completion, foreign/auxiliary/stale/replacement senders, duplicate/guessed callbacks, transition-time and late replies. Invalid replies leave the legitimate wait usable.
- [ ] Keep outgoing authorized services usable through actual cleanup. Valid final acknowledgement precedes revocation, which precedes replacement/native destruction. Crash/destruction/replacement during either phase retires waits as interrupted, without fabricated permission, completion or veto.
- [ ] Verify exact-document lifecycle readiness, stale/late readiness rejection, startup Close promptly reporting interruption, shared overlapping Close/direct-disposal/host outcomes, later explicit Close after readiness, and no automatic retry/replay when readiness arrives. Trace actual dispatch/receiver ordering.
- [ ] Distinguish genuine safeguard cancellation, interruption, cleanup failure and completed disposal throughout Close, direct disposal and host coordination. A later explicit attempt uses surviving state without replaying completed phases/notifications or reviving expired authority. Check affected reload and workspace-opening callers do not proceed after interrupted permission/cleanup.

### V3. Project recovery, Close precedence and complete disposal

- [ ] Crash and Reopen only the affected project; preserve shared host, Agents, healthy projects, extension hosts and representative work. Restore exact workspace/environment/profile and agreed recoverable state. Retire old views, registrations, listeners/callbacks/subscriptions and renderer-owned resources exactly once, without replaying requests.
- [ ] Force bootstrap/replacement failure and exercise Retry/Close, repeated recovery, Close during recovery, delayed success/failure/readiness and host shutdown during recovery. At most one recovery per project; no duplicate/orphan view, obsolete attachment/selection, closed-tab resurrection, stale authority or cancelled-recovery resumption.
- [ ] Preserve a pending project Close through genuine host-shutdown cancellation, immediately invalidate its recovery, and complete it after coordination releases ownership. Cover interrupted host coordination during permission and after partial cleanup; retire waits, retain/reconcile real surviving state and completed phases, and distinguish actual host loss.
- [ ] Exercise already-destroyed views, genuine cleanup errors, reentrant/overlapping Close and explicit retries. Independently safe cleanup continues after an error; real errors remain visible, completed phases/notifications do not repeat, and incomplete bookkeeping is not skipped because a registry entry vanished.
- [ ] Verify registry/count/listener/selection/restoration cleanup and native-host versus logical-workbench notifications. Expired projects reject and never alias shell/neighbour/replacement. Close remains pending through required cleanup; success reflects real logical teardown. Closing the final project leaves permanent Agents and host usable. Preserve independent provider work and exact-chat ownership.

### V4. Ordinary workspace, opening and app lifecycle

- [ ] Distinct workspace configuration/storage/trust/profiles/themes and extension-host commands; two projects sharing a profile retain existing profile-setting propagation. Agents/shell remain stable. Preserve documented layer direction.
- [ ] Dirty editors/layout, terminal heartbeat, task/debug progress and Git/workspace context survive repeated active/inactive switching. Save, terminals, Git, debugging and native-menu commands reach the selected project; Agents requires explicit project targets.
- [ ] Actual active/inactive/final project-tab Close and isolated reload; reopen recoverable state without restarting ended commands or agent requests. Whole-window Close/native close/app quit coordinate all safeguards, genuine veto and active work, with no orphaned views/processes. Record actual recovery/process effects rather than assuming process isolation.
- [ ] Fresh app-owned profile/extensions/shared storage, first-launch Agents, no legacy import; provider-history discovery remains distinct from profile import. Confirm other profiles are untouched. Exercise restored tab order/selection/recoverable state and unavailable local/worktree/remote targets with explicit Retry/Close while neighbours remain usable.
- [ ] Opening compatibility: New Window/new tab, Reuse Window, Open Agents, exact workspace activation, explicit launch target/profile, file/line and diff/merge arguments, selected startup preference modes and entry points. `--wait` follows the relevant files/workbench, not shell lifetime, switching or another project's closure. Untested combinations stay explicit.

## Stage 2 — exact chat and independent execution ownership

### V5. Real provider/tool/approval continuity

- [ ] Use a real Agent Host conversation from Agents and its home project's central chat editor. Record identical provider/session/exact-chat/home identity; sequential sends from either surface mutate the same provider authority. Navigation alone sends/claims/approves nothing; no mock transcript or competing persistent store.
- [ ] Switch while streaming, with unsent input, attachments/model/reading state and a pending approval, including before draft debounce. Count sends, approvals and tool executions to detect duplication/loss.
- [ ] Close and reload the home project during client-tool work. The same run and approval remain operable in Agents, then reopen the exact home/chat. Show the real tool/client/approval execution owner after closure without retaining the entire closed project workbench, losing its executor/observer, duplicating work or broadening trust/permissions.
- [ ] Exercise extension-backed Copilot Cloud continuation/ownership if available, recording provider/backend coverage. Credentials/service limits are unperformed checks with a provider-limited verdict under the original contract; Agent Host results cannot establish provider-wide support.

## Stage 3 — usability, failure and capacity

### V6. Native UX, real process allocation and measured cost

- [ ] Keyboard-only switching, native menus/dialog focus, IME composition and basic VoiceOver. Hidden projects must not remain keyboard/accessibility interaction targets; background attention must not steal focus.
- [ ] Actual renderer/process allocation, project/Agents/shell crash or unresponsive scope and recovery consequences, distinguishing native-host loss and provider execution-owner loss. No universal process-level isolation or replay claims from separate WebContents alone.
- [ ] Measure warm switching distributions against the roughly 200 ms goal and CPU/memory with 3–5 and ten projects, idle/active workloads and hidden/minimized/occluded states. Record machine/method and verify genuine terminal/task/agent progress. Do not suspend/close work to meet targets; do not invent numerical budgets before measurement.

## Evidence, environment scope and verdict

### V7. Acceptance accounting

- [ ] For every required scenario, record exact source/build/runtime, setup/run controls, assertions/logs/measurements, passed/failed/unperformed status, failures/repairs/reruns and injection limitations. Source inspection and frozen-evidence consistency checks are not runtime passes. Avoid counting prior samples at different commits as current-source coverage.
- [ ] Preserve initial macOS/local experiment scope, independent remote-authority architecture constraints and explicit Windows/Linux/SSH/Dev Container/provider limits. Actual remote diagnostics are distinct from synthetic authority. Do not silently claim untested support, silently exclude an accepted constraint or expand the original required runtime coverage by implication.
- [ ] Obtain the creator's separate live, scope-specific experiment verdict. Acceptance of an implementation rule or of the decision to continue investing is not acceptance of runtime feasibility. Runtime acceptance stays blocked until its required evidence and creator review exist. Final design approval is separate and does not certify this acceptance.

Existing creator constraints persist: provider sign-in/work was deferred and authorization probes are paused. This issue does not authorize lifting either. Work can be prepared or inspected within authorized scope; missing access remains explicit.

## Bounded execution protocol

Choose a single scenario group and precise baseline before each execution batch; state the controls, expected observable result and stopping point. Correct missing implementation via its owning issue, then rerun the affected requirements. A failure blocks acceptance but not authorized investigation. Do not automatically roll another subsystem into the same batch or convert every failed test into a new architecture ticket.

Only a demonstrated contract conflict or a real design trade-off returns to Wayfinder with a precise question, alternatives and evidence. Preserve this runtime acceptance gate and its native necessary-integration dependency through any such return. Design-map closure remains separate from runtime acceptance. No production merge or automatic scheduling is requested.
title: Validate retained-view hosting against the full accepted contract
